T.Naveen Sc, Kerala State Pollution Control Board, Other Present: Gp- Riyal Devassy This Writ Petition (Civil) Having Been Finally Heard On 29.10.2025 , The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following: W.P.(C).No.4506 of 2021 3 2025:Ker:81319 Viju Abraham, J. -------------------- W.P.(C).No.4506 of 2021 -------------------------------- Dated this the 29th day of October, 2025 Judgment Petitioner has approached this Court seeking a direction to respondents 2 and 4 to take proper action against the 5th respondent so as to implement Ext.P2 order of the 2nd respondent. 2. The grievance
texts.facts: raised by the petitioner is that though the 2nd respondent has cancelled the licence granted to the 5th respondent as per Ext.P2 on finding that the 5th respondent has been conducting Jose P.V vs Nedumbassery Grama Panchayath on 29 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136935433/ 2 illegal business other than the purpose for which the licence was granted, no further follow up action was taken by the 2nd respondent to stop the functioning of the business conducted by the 5th respondent. It is averred that the 5th respondent is conducting the work of dismantling old vehicles and recycling spare parts from the dismantled vehicles; the oil and grease emanate from the 5th respondent's workshop which causes serious pollution to the water sources. Petitioner 2025:KER:81319 would submit that based on the complaint, Ext.P2 order was issued as early as 06.12.2019, whereby the licence granted to the 5th respondent was cancelled and a direction was issued to stop the functioning of the business activity undertaken by the 5th respondent. Though the 5th respondent has approached this Court filing WP(C)9788 of 2020 seeking to renew the licence granted by the Grama Panchayat and challenging the stop memo, this Court, by Ext.P5 order, directed consideration of the application for renewal submitted by the 5 th respondent, but with a rider that the petitioner shall not be permitted to conduct any business in the building in question pending consideration of the renewal application. Pursuant to the direction issued by this Court, an inspection was conducted by the Pollution Control Board. 5. It is admitted by the 2nd respondent that they have issued Ext.P2 order whereby the licence granted to the 5th respondent has been cancelled, and also directed the 5th respondent to stop the functioning of the business undertaken by the petitioner. From the report submitted by the Pollution Control Board, it is discernible that in spite of the issuance of Ext.P2, the 5th respondent is running the unit. The learned counsel for the respondent Panchayath submits that till date the licence has not been renewed or issued afresh.
texts.arguments: 3. The learned counsel appearing for the 5th respondent would submit that it is true that the licence granted has been revoked as per Ext.P2 and no fresh licence has been issued till date.
